102	 * this custom attribute, only a generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, so this documents
103	 * the real, confirmed-live shape (see this module's own docblock's "Badge" section) rather than
104	 * reading through `any`. Not otherwise an augmentation — everything else this mapper reads is
105	 * already typed by the SDK — so this stays close to "a plain alias" in spirit, just no longer
106	 * literally one.
107	 */
108	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
109	  // productBadgeUrl is real, confirmed-live data (see this module's own docblock's "Badge"
110	  // section) but genuinely unused below -- typed anyway so a test fixture built from the real
111	  // wire shape doesn't have to omit it to satisfy this type.
112	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string; productBadgeUrl?: string }>;
113	};
114	
115	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl —
116	 *  same shape as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `FormatPrice`, redeclared locally for the same
117	 *  separate-module reason as `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct` above. */
118	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
119	
120	/**
121	 * The full `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard` props this mapper produces — badge, size chips,
122	 * was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, heading level and variation all included. Mirrors
123	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` (unexported from that file, so
124	 * redeclared here rather than imported) — this mapper's output is meant to be spread straight
125	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` by its page container (SFCC-84's Full History page, not yet built)
126	 * with nothing left to add, the same convenience that shape already gives PLP's own page.
127	 */
128	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
129	
130	/** The correctly-sized product image view for the required `primaryImage` slot — same constant,
131	 *  same reasoning, as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`: never serve an
132	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance). */
133	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
134	
135	/** The variation-attribute id this mapper reads for size chips — named per conventions.md's
136	 *  no-magic-strings rule. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectSizeChipValues`, which this is
137	 *  ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file. */
138	const SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'size';
139	
140	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
141	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
142	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
143	
144	/**
145	 * Resolves which real colour this product's images should come from. Only the fallback half of
146	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` — there is no `representedProduct`
147	 * branch here because this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` (from `getProducts`),
148	 * which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type, same as
149	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s identical `resolveViewedColour`): first orderable variant, else the
150	 * first variant, is the only strategy available to this mapper. Returns `undefined` when there are
151	 * no variants at all — `selectColourScopedImages` below then falls back to an unscoped,
152	 * viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
153	 */
154	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): string | undefined => {
155	  const fallbackVariant = product.variants?.find((variant) => variant.orderable) ?? product.variants?.[0];
156	  return fallbackVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
157	};
158	
159	/**
160	 * Extracts the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into a catalog image's own filename
161	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`). Mirrors
162	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own helper of the same name exactly, same real bug: the array order
163	 * `filterImageGroups` hands back is not guaranteed to match this sequence — confirmed live on
164	 * `4673TS251`, whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`. Returns `undefined` for
165	 * a non-numeric filename; `sortByImageSequence` leaves those untouched.
166	 */
167	const extractImageSequenceNumber = (src: string): number | undefined => {
168	  const filename = src.split('/').pop() ?? '';
169	  const match = /^(\d+)\./.exec(filename);
170	  return match ? Number(match[1]) : undefined;
171	};
172	
173	/** Stable sort by `extractImageSequenceNumber` (guaranteed stable since ES2019) — images with no
174	 *  numeric filename compare equal and keep their original relative order. */
175	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ZimmProductCardImage[]): ZimmProductCardImage[] =>
176	  [...images].sort((a, b) => {
177	    const numA = extractImageSequenceNumber(a.src);
178	    const numB = extractImageSequenceNumber(b.src);
179	    if (numA === undefined || numB === undefined) return 0;
180	    return numA - numB;
181	  });
182	
183	/**
184	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
185	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
186	 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s
187	 * catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`, a shorthand ambient module
188	 * declaration that types the whole module `any`, so `getPriceData`'s real return is implicitly
189	 * `any`. Declaring a local, narrow type for the fields actually read — rather than letting that
190	 * `any` propagate into this module's own types — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
191	 * narrow-local-type pattern for the same untyped function (typescript.md's no-`any` rule). This
192	 * is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee: TypeScript allows
193	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
194	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
195	 */
196	type SfccPriceData = {
197	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
198	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
199	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
200	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
201	  currentPrice: number;
202	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
203	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
204	  listPrice: number | undefined;
205	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
206	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */
207	  isOnSale: boolean;
208	};
209	
210	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
211	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
212	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
213	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
214	 *  already exports). */
215	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
216	
217	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
218	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
219	  if (!src) return undefined;
220	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
221	};
222	
223	/**
224	 * The colour + `medium`-viewtype-scoped image list this product's card uses — one lookup feeding
225	 * four separate things below (`primaryImage`, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the
226	 * broken-image fallback candidates), so none of them can ever disagree with each other or with the
227	 * resolved colour. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
228	 * `selectColourScopedImages`, re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape)
229	 * in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`
230	 * types are identical either way (confirmed directly against
231	 * `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`).
232	 *
233	 * **Two-pass, not one** — same real bug as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own version closes: a
234	 * strict colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` match requires the group to explicitly declare a
235	 * matching `variationAttributes` entry, but a single-colour product's medium group commonly
236	 * carries no `variationAttributes` at all (nothing to disambiguate), which would make a
237	 * colour-scoped-only lookup exclude the group and return nothing. Falls back to a viewtype-only
238	 * match in that case. Never the reverse — a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
239	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
240	 */
241	const selectColourScopedImages = (
242	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
243	  colour: string | undefined,
244	): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
245	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
246	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
247	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
248	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
249	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
250	    : [];
251	
252	  const groups =
253	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
254	      ? colourScopedGroups
255	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
256	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
257	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
258	
259	  const images = (groups[0]?.images ?? [])
260	    .map(toCardImage)
261	    .filter((image): image is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(image));
262	
263	  return sortByImageSequence(images);
264	};
265	
266	/**
267	 * Picks this product's gallery from the colour-scoped image list above — matches
268	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for 0 or 1 images (returns `undefined`, never
269	 * a 1-length array). Kept exported and independently tested, same as
270	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
271	 * below calls `selectColourScopedImages` directly instead (one shared computation feeding
272	 * `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`/`hoverImage`/`images` at once), matching that file's own
273	 * documented, deliberate minor redundancy rather than introducing a new one.
274	 */
275	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
276	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
277	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
278	};
279	
280	/**
281	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
282	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
283	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
284	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
285	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
286	 */
287	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
288	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
289	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
290	    value: value.value,
291	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
292	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
293	  }));
294	};
295	
296	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — same shape, same
297	 *  reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ResolvedVariant`: the real, orderable SKU for
298	 *  that specific size, not the master id this product otherwise defaults to. */
299	export type ResolvedVariant = {
300	  productId: string;
301	  price: number | undefined;
302	  orderable: boolean;
303	};
304	
305	/**
306	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — ported near-verbatim from
307	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveOrderableVariant`, re-pointed at this input's own
308	 * `variants` field (identical shape either way — both are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `Variant`
309	 * types). Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all — callers fall back to this
310	 * product's own default id/price in that case, the same default that already existed before
311	 * size-aware Add to Bag was ever selectable.
312	 */
313	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (
314	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
315	  sizeValue: string,
316	): ResolvedVariant | null => {
317	  const variant = product.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
318	  if (!variant) return null;
319	
320	  return {
321	    productId: variant.productId,
322	    price: variant.price,
323	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
324	  };
325	};
326	
327	/**
328	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
329	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
330	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
331	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
332	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
333	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
334	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
335	 */
336	const selectPriceFields = (
337	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
338	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
339	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
340	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
341	
342	  const currentPrice =
343	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
344	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
345	      : undefined;
346	
347	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
348	  // identical to its current one.
349	  const originalPrice =
350	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
351	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
352	      : undefined;
353	
354	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
355	};
356	
357	/**
358	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
359	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
360	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
361	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
362	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
363	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
364	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
365	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
366	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
367	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
368	 */
369	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
370	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
371	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
372	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
373	  if (!product?.name) return null;
374	
375	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
376	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
377	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
378	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
379	  if (!firstImage) return null;
380	
381	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — mirrors this mapper's own established
382	  // fallback (and recentlyViewedCard.ts's identical one) exactly. The rest of scopedImages keeps
383	  // toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery images, which get no
384	  // such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this extra safeguard.
385	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: firstImage.alt || product.name };
386	
387	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
388	
389	  return {
390	    id: product.id,
391	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
392	    name: product.name,
393	    headingLevel: 'h3',
394	    primaryImage,
395	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
396	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
397	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
398	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
399	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
400	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
401	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
402	    currentPrice,
403	    originalPrice,
404	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
405	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
406	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
407	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
408	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
409	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
410	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
411	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
412	    variation: 'plp',
413	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
414	  };
415	};
